Shiny bindings for govReactable Output and render functions for using govReactable within shiny apps

Source: R/govReactable.R
govReactable-shiny.Rd

Shiny bindings for govReactable Output and render functions for using govReactable within shiny apps

Usage

govReactableOutput(
  output_table_name,
  caption,
  caption_size = "l",
  heading_level = 2L,
  subtitle = NULL
)

renderGovReactable(expr, env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE)

Arguments

output_table_name

Output variable to read from

caption

Adds a caption heading that screen readers link to the table. Plain text is escaped and shown as written; use shiny::HTML() or tags for markup. The heading's id is output_table_name plus -caption, and the subtitle's is -subtitle. To change either from the server, use update_reactable_caption()

caption_size

Size of the caption: "s", "m", "l" (default) or "xl". Any other value is an error.

heading_level

The caption's heading level, an integer from 1L to 5L. Defaults to 2L. Use 1L when the table is the main content of the page. Strings such as "h3" are as of shinyGovstyle 0.3.0 and will stop working in 1.0.0; use an integer (for example 3L) instead.

subtitle

Optional line under the caption, in smaller, lighter text: what the data is, where and when it covers, and the units if every value shares them (e.g. "Cost of bikes (£), England, 2025"). It becomes part of the table's accessible name, with the caption. Needs a caption. Plain text is escaped and shown as written; use shiny::HTML() or tags for markup. NULL (default) shows no subtitle

expr

An expression that generates a reactable widget

env

The environment in which to evaluate expr

quoted

Is expr a quoted expression (with quote())? This is useful if you want to save an expression in a variable

Value

govReactableOutput() returns a reactable output element that can be included in a Shiny UI

renderGovReactable() returns a reactable render function that can be assigned to a Shiny output slot

Table titles

Every table needs a title. The Analysis Function guidance on tables suggests two parts, which match two arguments:

  • caption: a short headline stating the message, e.g. "Costs peaked in March".

  • subtitle: what the data is, where and when, e.g. "Cost of bikes, vans and buses (£), England, January to May 2025". Include the units if every value shares them.

A headline is optional. Without one, put the what, where and when in caption and leave out subtitle.

Put the source of the data under the table (for example with gov_text()), not in the title.

Screen reader users hear the caption and subtitle together when they reach the table, so keep them short and don't repeat information. See also the GOV.UK Design System table component.

See also

Other Govstyle tables tabs and accordions: accordion(), govReactable(), govTable(), govTabs(), update_reactable_caption()

Examples

ui <- shinyGovstyle::gov_page(
  govReactableOutput(
    "table",
    caption = "Virginica flowers have the longest petals",
    subtitle = "Petal and sepal measurements (cm) for three iris species"
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$table <- renderGovReactable({
    # Longest petals first, so the top rows show what the caption says
    govReactable(iris[order(iris$Petal.Length, decreasing = TRUE), ])
  })
}

if (interactive()) shinyApp(ui, server)

# A caption that changes with a filter. The starting caption matches the
# dropdown's default.
species <- levels(iris$Species)

ui <- shinyGovstyle::gov_page(
  shinyGovstyle::select_Input(
    inputId = "species",
    label = "Species",
    select_text = species,
    select_value = species
  ),
  govReactableOutput(
    "table",
    caption = paste(species[1], "measurements")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$table <- renderGovReactable({
    govReactable(iris[iris$Species == input$species, ])
  })

  shiny::observe({
    update_reactable_caption(
      session,
      "table",
      paste(input$species, "measurements")
    )
  })
}

if (interactive()) shinyApp(ui, server)
